consent.title: One quick question
consent.what: Ember saves your habit names, check-ins, low days, day notes and moods. They can say something about your health (think "take my meds" or "sleep 8 hours"). Under the GDPR (Article 9) that counts as health data, so Ember asks before saving it.
consent.why: Ember stores it only to run your habit tracker for you. It's never sold or used for ads. It reaches only the services that run Ember (for example Discord, if you use it for reminders, and our hosting and email providers). The privacy policy lists them. You can change your mind any time by deleting your account in Settings, which removes everything.
consent.without: Without it you can still read your history, change settings, and export or delete your data.

about.intro: Ember is a calm companion for hard moments and gentle days: a short practice when things get too big, and gentle habits for the rest.
about.moment.heading: When a moment gets too big
about.moment.text: Tap “I need a moment”. Ember asks what's going on and walks you through a short practice, like slow breathing or 5-4-3-2-1. It works without an account and offline. Nothing from it is saved unless you choose to keep a note in your private journal.
about.habits.heading: On the other days
about.habits.text: Gentle habits: small things like a glass of water or ten pages of reading, with friendly reminders. A rough day doesn't count against you. Mark it as a low day or check in later, and streaks are up to you. There's a journal with moods too, end-to-end encrypted if you like.
about.privacy.heading: Your data
about.privacy.text: With an account, your habits stay in sync on the web, in the Android app and in Discord. Without one, your data stays on this device only.
about.beta: Ember is still in beta and isn't a medical service. In an emergency, call 112.
landing.lede: {{description}} When it gets loud, Ember stays with you for a few steady minutes: name what's happening, breathe, ride it out. No account needed, and nothing from a moment is kept unless you choose to save it.
landing.talk: Need someone to talk to right now?
landing.madeBy: Free. Made by Nico, a developer in Germany.
landing.screenshotAlt: Ember's Today screen: the “I need a moment” door above the habits, three of them checked in today.
landing.feature.reminders.title: Reminders that nudge, not nag
landing.feature.reminders.text: A notification at the times you pick, with a Done button right in it. Yesterday stays open, so a forgotten check-in is easy to fill in.
landing.feature.platforms.title: On the web and on Android
landing.feature.platforms.text: Check in from any browser, or use the Android app with reminders that work offline and a home-screen widget.
landing.feature.flexible.title: Habits that bend
landing.feature.flexible.text: Daily, weekdays, a few times a week or several times a day. Call a hard day a low day. Streaks stay off unless you want them.
landing.feature.private.title: Private by design
landing.feature.private.text: Try it without an account and your data stays on this device. Keep an end-to-end encrypted journal, and export everything any time.
landing.extra.journal.title: A journal and moods
landing.extra.journal.text: Jot a line about your day and pick how it felt. Add your own moods next to the five built-in ones.
landing.extra.themes.title: Four themes, light and dark
landing.extra.themes.text: Hearthlight, Fieldnotes, Tidepool and Marigold, each in light and dark. Pick the one that feels like yours.
landing.extra.discord.title: Use Discord? Bring Ember along
landing.extra.discord.text: If you like, add the Ember bot for reminders in your DMs and quick check-ins there. You can sign in with Discord too.

history.pickDay: Pick a day to fill it in or change it.
history.announce.lowDayOff: {{date}} is no longer a low day.
history.view.label: History view
day.choices: Not done notes that you let this day go. Clear leaves it empty, as if nothing was entered.
day.lowDayAll: Low days apply to all your habits.
year.title: Your year
year.lede: Every day you showed up, across the last 12 months. Tap a day for more.
year.empty.body: Once you have a habit, your year fills in here.
year.showedUp_one: You showed up {{showed}} of the last {{count}} day.
year.showedUp_other: You showed up {{showed}} of the last {{count}} days.
year.moodsHidden: Moods stay hidden while your private journal is locked on this device.
year.words.showedUpPartly: you showed up, {{done}} of {{scheduled}} done, {{partial}} partly
year.scrollHint: Earlier months are to the left. Scroll sideways to see them.
year.tableLabel: Your last 12 months, one column per week
journal.locked: Your private journal is locked on this device.
journal.expired: That took a while, so the journal locked again. Unlock it with your recovery code once more.
journal.heading: How was {{date}}?
journal.privacy: Only you see this. It never appears in reminders.
journal.recoveryNewPassphrase: Your recovery code worked. Choose a new passphrase to finish unlocking; your recovery code stays the same.
journal.newPassphraseSet: Your new passphrase is set. Your journal is unlocked on this device.
journal.tooLong: Keep it to {{max}} characters or fewer.
journal.queued: Saved on this device, it'll sync when you're back online.
moods.nameTooLong: Keep it to 24 characters or fewer.
moods.emojiInvalid: Use a single emoji, or leave this empty.
moods.limit: You have 20 moods in use. Archive one to make room for another.
moods.name: Name
moods.locked: Your own moods are in your private journal, which is locked on this device.
moods.intro: Add your own moods next to the five built-in ones. Archiving hides a mood from the picker; days you already gave it keep showing it.
journal.error.tooLong: Keep the entry to 2000 characters or fewer.
journal.error.moodName: Give the mood a name of up to 24 characters.
journal.error.cipherTooLong: That entry is too long to save.
journal.error.locked: The private journal is locked on this device.
settings.group.appearanceSummary: Language, light or dark, your theme and calm mode
settings.group.feedbackSummary: Tell us what would make Ember better
settings.group.helpSummary: Crisis lines, any time of day
settings.moments.intro: The reflections you saved after a moment, read on this device from your private journal.
helps.intro: A short list of what helped you before. The first few show up when you open “I need a moment”. Only you can read it.
helps.needsPrivate: This list is kept in your private journal, so only you can read it. Turn the private journal on to start one.
helps.needsAccount: This list needs an account with the private journal, so only you can read it.
helps.locked: Your private journal is locked on this device. Unlock it to see this list.
helps.loadFailed: Your list didn't load. Check your connection and try again.
helps.empty: Nothing here yet. Add something below, or from Your moments.
helps.newHint: For example: a walk around the block, or calling a friend.
helps.full: That's {{max}}, the most the list keeps. Remove one to make room.
helps.already: “{{text}}” is already in What helps me.
helps.error.full: Your list holds {{max}} things, the most it keeps. Remove one to make room.
helps.error.conflict: Another device changed your list at the same time. Try again in a moment.
helps.error.save: That didn't save. Check your connection and try again.
settings.passwordMismatch: That password doesn't match. Try again.
settings.discord.outcome.linked: Discord is linked. You can sign in with it from now on.
settings.discord.outcome.conflict: Ember couldn't link that Discord account. It may already belong to another Ember account that has a password. Or this account is already linked to a different Discord account.
settings.discord.outcome.error: Linking didn't finish. You can try again.
settings.discord.outcome.password: Ember needs your password before linking Discord. You can try again here.
settings.discord.unlinked: Discord is unlinked. You can link it again any time.
settings.discord.linkedText: Your Discord account is linked. You can sign in with it, and the Ember bot knows it's you.
settings.discord.intro: Use Discord? Link it to sign in with Discord and to use the Ember bot with the same habits.
settings.discord.passwordHint: Ember checks it before linking Discord.
settings.discord.nativeHint: Linking happens in your browser. Come back here afterwards and Ember picks it up.
settings.account.everywhereConfirm: This signs you out on every device, including this one.
settings.account.passwordSent: We sent a link to {{email}}. Open it to choose a new password. It can take a minute or two to arrive.
settings.account.signOutFailed: Ember couldn't sign you out. Check your connection and try again.
settings.account.everywhereFailed: Ember couldn't sign you out everywhere. Check your connection and try again.
settings.appearance.hintAccount: Choose how Ember looks. Your theme follows you to your other devices.
settings.appearance.notSaved: Your new look is set on this device. We couldn't save it to your account just now, so your other devices keep theirs for now.
settings.colorScheme.label: Light or dark
settings.colorScheme.hint: System follows your device. This choice stays on this device.
themes.hearthlight: Candle-lit kitchen table: warm, soft, familiar.
themes.tidepool: Morning by the water: cool, airy, unhurried.
themes.marigold: Sticker sheet: playful, confident, high contrast.
settings.push.intro: These are the places Ember can remind you. Each habit and routine uses all of them unless you untick one when you edit it. Switch a place off and nothing reminds you there.
settings.push.stillOn: That didn't save, so {{name}} is still on. Try again in a moment.
settings.push.stillOff: That didn't save, so {{name}} is still off. Try again in a moment.
settings.push.noneDiscord: If you use Discord, you can link it in <anchor>Account & security</anchor>.
settings.push.loading: Loading where Ember can remind you…
settings.push.browserHint: Reminders can show in this browser too, even when Ember isn't open. By default a notification doesn't name your habit, since it can show on a lock screen.
settings.push.iosHint: On iPhone and iPad, notifications work once Ember is on your Home Screen: tap Share, choose "Add to Home Screen", then open Ember from there.
settings.push.turnOn: Turn on reminders in this browser
settings.push.on: Notifications are on. Reminders can now reach this device.
settings.push.denied: Your browser is blocking notifications from Ember. To allow them, open the site settings (often the icon next to the address bar), set Notifications to Allow, then try again.
settings.push.failed: Notifications couldn't be turned on in this browser. You can try again.
settings.dm.paused: Ember paused your Discord DM reminders because they couldn't be delivered. This often happens when DMs from server members are turned off. Once DMs can reach you again, you can turn them back on.
settings.phone.introLocal: Turn on "Remind me on this phone" for a habit when you edit it. Reminders are set on this phone, so they arrive even without a connection.
settings.phone.intro: Reminders are set on this phone, so they arrive even without a connection.
settings.phone.late: Reminders can arrive up to an hour late until you allow "Alarms & reminders" for Ember in your phone's settings.
settings.phone.notificationsOff: Notifications are off for Ember on this phone. You can turn them on in your phone's settings.
settings.phone.turnOn: Turn on reminders on this phone
settings.phone.on: Reminders are on for this phone.
settings.reminderNames.label: Show habit names in reminders
settings.reminderNames.hint: Reminders can show on your lock screen, so by default they only say "Ember". With names on, they say which habit or routine is due.
settings.second.hint: If you haven't checked in yet, Ember nudges you once more.
settings.routines.intro: Group habits that belong together into routines, like a morning routine.
settings.streaks.label: Show streaks
settings.streaks.hint: Counts the days in a row you kept a habit, on Today and in History. Off, Ember shows your check-ins without counting.
settings.calm.label: Calm mode
settings.calm.hint: No motion, softer colors and fewer decorations. Breathing shows text only.
settings.grace.label: Grace days per week
settings.grace.hint: Up to this many days a week can pass without a check-in and your streak keeps going. Every check-in counts, no matter the gap.
settings.grace.note: Grace days happen on their own. A low day is one you mark yourself, and a pause is for one habit.
settings.timezone.follows: Your days follow {{zone}}. Reminders and "today" use this timezone.
settings.timezone.notSet: You haven't picked a timezone yet, so Ember uses {{zone}} for now. Reminders and "today" follow it.
settings.timezone.label: Choose a timezone
settings.timezone.hint: Start typing a city or region, like Berlin or New York.
settings.timezone.empty: Pick a timezone, or start typing a city.
settings.timezone.unknown: Ember doesn't know that timezone. Pick one from the list.
export.intro: Download everything Ember keeps about you: your settings, every habit (paused ones too), all check-ins and low days, your email and your Discord ID. JSON is handy for other apps, CSV opens in a spreadsheet.
settings.delete.intro: This removes your account and everything in it: habits, check-ins, low days and settings. It can't be undone. If you'd like to keep a copy, download your data first.
settings.delete.typeDeleteCaps: Type DELETE in capital letters to confirm.
twoFactor.code.empty: Enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app.
twoFactor.code.wrong: That code didn't work. Codes change every 30 seconds, so try the newest one.
twoFactor.code.label: Code from your authenticator app
twoFactor.recovery.empty: Enter one of your recovery codes.
twoFactor.passwordHint: Ember checks it before turning on two-step sign-in.
twoFactor.copyFailed: Copying didn't work here. Select the text and copy it instead.
twoFactor.codes.fileHeading: Ember recovery codes. Each one works once.
twoFactor.codes.heading: Your recovery codes
twoFactor.codes.text: Keep these somewhere safe; each works once. If you lose your phone, a recovery code signs you in instead of the authenticator code. You won't see them again here.
twoFactor.setup.step1: 1. Add Ember to your authenticator app
twoFactor.setup.scan: Scan this code with an authenticator app on your phone, such as Aegis, 2FAS or Google Authenticator.
twoFactor.setup.qrLabel: QR code for adding Ember to your authenticator app
twoFactor.setup.cantScan: Can't scan it? Enter this key in the app instead.
twoFactor.on: Two-step sign-in is on. After your password, Ember asks for a code from your authenticator app.
twoFactor.regenerateHint: New codes replace your old ones.
twoFactor.disableHintPassword: To turn it off, confirm with your password.
twoFactor.disableHintCode: To turn it off, confirm with a current code.
twoFactor.intro: Add a second step when you sign in: after your password, Ember asks for a 6-digit code from an authenticator app on your phone. It protects your sign-in; your private journal has its own lock.
twoFactor.offDone: Two-step sign-in is off. Your password alone signs you in again.
twoFactor.codesSavedDone: Recovery codes saved. Keep them safe.
journalSettings.passphrase.short: Use at least 10 characters. A few words make a good passphrase.
journalSettings.passphrase.mismatch: The two passphrases don't match yet.
journalSettings.passphrase.label: Journal passphrase
journalSettings.passphrase.hint: At least 10 characters. Pick something different from your login password.
journalSettings.passphrase.wrong: That passphrase doesn't open your journal. Check it and try again.
journalSettings.recovery.wrong: That recovery code doesn't open your journal. Check it and try again.
journalSettings.recovery.label: Recovery code
journalSettings.recovery.hint: 8 groups of 4 letters and numbers. Spaces and dashes are fine.
journalSettings.loginPassword.label: Your login password
journalSettings.loginPassword.hint: Ember checks it to make sure it’s you.
journalSettings.loginPassword.mismatch: That login password doesn't match. Try again.
journalSettings.problem.locked: Your journal is locked on this device again. Unlock it, then try once more.
journalSettings.problem.device: Something went wrong on this device. You can try again.
journalSettings.remember.label: Remember on this device
journalSettings.remember.hint: Stay unlocked here until you sign out. Leave it off on a shared device.
journalSettings.recoveryStep.tick: Tick this once your recovery code is somewhere safe.
journalSettings.recoveryStep.heading: Your private journal is on
journalSettings.recoveryStep.text: Here is your recovery code. It opens your journal if you forget your passphrase. Write it down or keep it in a password manager: you'll only see it now.
journalSettings.readable.names: habit and routine names (the Discord bot and reminders need them)
journalSettings.expired: That took a while, so the journal locked again. Unlock it with your recovery code once more.
journalSettings.lockedDone: Your journal is locked on this device. Unlock it with your passphrase whenever you like.
journalSettings.encrypting_one: Encrypting your journal: 1 entry or mood to go.
journalSettings.encrypting_other: Encrypting your journal: {{count}} entries and moods to go.
journalSettings.decrypting_one: Decrypting your journal: 1 entry or mood to go.
journalSettings.decrypting_other: Decrypting your journal: {{count}} entries and moods to go.
journalSettings.recoveryWorked: Your recovery code worked. Choose a new passphrase to finish unlocking; your recovery code stays the same.
journalSettings.newPassphraseDone: Your new passphrase is set. Your journal is unlocked on this device.
journalSettings.offIntro: Your journal is already private to your account. The private journal goes one step further: entries and your own moods are encrypted on your device before they're sent, so only you can read them. Not even Ember's server can.
journalSettings.readableIntro: What Ember's server can still read, by design:
journalSettings.keepSafe.heading: Keep two things safe
journalSettings.keepSafe.text: Your passphrase and a recovery code (shown once) are the only ways in. If you lose both, nobody can open your journal again, Ember included. You could only delete it and start fresh.
journalSettings.lockedTurningOff: Ember is turning your private journal back into a plain one. Unlock it on this device to carry on.
journalSettings.locked: Your private journal is locked on this device. Unlock it to read and write entries here.
journalSettings.discard.heading: Delete the private journal
journalSettings.discard.text: This deletes every private journal entry and your own moods for good, then turns the private journal off. Your habits, check-ins and low days stay.
journalSettings.discard.done: Your private journal is deleted and turned off. You can start a fresh one any time.
journalSettings.unlockedDone: Your journal is unlocked on this device.
journalSettings.lostBoth: I lost both my passphrase and recovery code
journalSettings.finishOff.heading: Turning your private journal off
journalSettings.finishOff.text: Your entries and own moods are being decrypted on this device and saved to your account readable again. Confirm to finish.
journalSettings.offDone: The private journal is off. Your entries are back to normal.
journalSettings.unlocked: Your private journal is on and unlocked on this device. Entries and your own moods are encrypted here before they're sent.
journalSettings.disableText: Your entries and own moods are decrypted on this device and saved to your account readable again, like before. Notes from "I need a moment" are re-uploaded as plain text too.
journalSettings.exportHint: The file isn't encrypted, so keep it somewhere private.
feedback.page.lede: Ember is in beta, and every note helps make it kinder and simpler.
feedback.pictures.none: Up to 5 pictures, 10 MB together. Screenshots help a lot.
feedback.pictures.full: That's 5 pictures, the most one report can carry. Remove one to add another.
feedback.pictures.room_one: Only 1 more picture fits, so the rest weren't added.
feedback.pictures.room_other: Only {{count}} more pictures fit, so the rest weren't added.
feedback.pictures.unreadable: {{name}} couldn't be opened as a picture. A JPEG, PNG or WebP works.
feedback.pictures.tooBig: {{name}} would go over 10 MB together, so it wasn't added.
feedback.pictures.why: Pictures you add help us fix the problem; we keep them until it's handled.
feedback.pictures.check: Check your screenshot first: please don't send notes, moods or anything about your health or other people.
feedback.pictures.accountOnly: With an account you can add pictures too.
feedback.tooManyPictures: Ember has had a lot of feedback and pictures in a short time. Please try again a little later, or send just the text. Your words and pictures are still here.
feedback.tooMany: Ember has had a lot of feedback in a short time. Please try again a little later, your text is still here.
feedback.sent.heading: Thank you, that really helps.
feedback.sent.text: Your feedback is on its way to the Ember team.
feedback.title.label: Title
feedback.title.hint: A few words, like "Reminder came late".
feedback.description.label: Description
feedback.description.hint: What would make Ember better? Ideas, bugs, or anything that got in your way.
feedback.anonymous.label: Send feedback anonymously
feedback.anonymous.hint: Leaves your account off this report.
feedback.sends.account: Ember sends the title, description and any pictures, the app version, the time and whether you use the web or the Android app. Your account goes with it unless you send anonymously. Never your habits or check-ins, and please keep private entries and other people out of pictures.
feedback.sends.plain: Ember sends the title, description, the app version, the time and whether you use the web or the Android app, plus your account if you're signed in. Never your habits or check-ins.
journal.error.wrongSecret: That passphrase or recovery code doesn't open the journal.
